rows.comments: The source explicitly states the March 2025 estimate of 18.6 million illegal aliens, matching the claim.
rows.source_quote: As of March 2025, FAIR estimates that approximately 18.6 million illegal aliens reside in the United States.

rows.comments: The source text provides figures for immigrants alone (50.2 million, 14.8 %) but does not mention the combined total of immigrants and their U.S.-born children, nor the 93 million or 28 % figure.
The source text does not provide any information about the United States’ share of the global population or the percentage of all international migrants residing in the United States.
The table lists 1,183,505 total legal immigrants, with 565,427 status adjustments and 618,078 new arrivals, matching the claim’s figures.
rows.source_quote: Total, all immigrants 1,183,505 565,427 618,078

rows.comments: The source confirms the 53.3 million figure and 15.8% share as record highs, but it does not state that the U.S. has the largest immigrant population in the world, nor does it explicitly claim immigration has been a major source of population growth and cultural change throughout U.S. history.
rows.source_quote: the foreign‑born or immigrant population (legal and illegal together) hit 53.3 million and 15.8 percent of the total U.S. population in January 2025 — both new record highs.

rows.comments: The source text lists detailed classes of admission for lawful permanent residents but does not mention persons admitted under the Nicaraguan and Central American Relief Act, children born after a parent's visa issuance, or parolees from the former Soviet Union, Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam denied refugee status.
The source text contains a table of lawful permanent resident admissions but does not mention Special Immigrant Visas for Iraqis and Afghans or a 1.0% figure.

The source confirms the 45%, 27%, and 23% figures and the 10.5‑million number for unauthorized immigrants, but it reports 5% temporary residents (not 6%) and does not provide the exact naturalized or permanent resident counts cited in the claim.
rows.source_quote: In 2017, 45% were naturalized U.S. citizens. Some 27% of immigrants were permanent residents and 5% were temporary residents in 2017. Another 23% of all immigrants were unauthorized immigrants. ... 10.5 million unauthorized immigrants in the U.S. in 2017.

rows.comments: The source confirms the September 2021 figure but does not mention a March 2018 estimate of 45.3 million or the claim about the lowest three‑year increase.
rows.source_quote: Figure 1 shows that the nation’s immigrant population grew to 45.4 million in September 2021, a 1.6 million increase since September 2020.

rows.comments: The source explicitly describes per‑country limits for family‑sponsored and employment‑based preference visas, confirming the claim.
rows.source_quote: The maximum number of family-sponsored and employment-based preference visas that can be issued to citizens of any country in a fiscal year. No more than 7 percent of the visas may be issued to natives of any one independent country in a fiscal year; no more than 2 percent may be issued to any one dependency of any independent country.

rows.comments: The source explicitly states that the U.S. had led the world for decades, admitting more refugees each year than all other countries combined, directly supporting the claim.
rows.source_quote: It had previously led the world on this measure for decades, admitting more refugees each year than all other countries combined.

rows.comments: The article explicitly links poverty and crime as conditions that drive people to migrate.
rows.source_quote: Yet two-thirds of Hondurans live in poverty ... Protected by government officials, criminal gangs have spread throughout the region, adding threats of kidnapping, extortion, rape, and murder to the daily life of people struggling to make a living.

rows.comments: The source explicitly states that between one half and two thirds of all immigrants to Colonial America were indentured servants, directly supporting the claim.
rows.source_quote: One half to two thirds of all immigrants to Colonial America arrived as indentured servants.

rows.comments: The article explicitly cites poverty and murder (crime) as driving forces behind migration.
rows.source_quote: Much of the poverty, injustice and murder in El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras is homegrown, harking back to the age of Spanish conquest ... Small criminal elites have long prospered at the expense of the populations.

rows.comments: The provided source text contains only a Wayback Machine capture link and metadata, with no actual content from the 1909 report to verify the claim.
The source explicitly states that historians estimate fewer than one million European immigrants arrived between 1600 and 1799.
rows.source_quote: Historians estimate that well under a million immigrants—perhaps as few as 400,000—crossed the Atlantic during those two centuries, and some scholars believe that the growth of the nation’s population—3,900,000 in the first census of 1790—was largely the result of natural increase and not of a great influx of the foreign-born.

rows.comments: The source text does not mention the Page Act of 1875, Chinese women, or any related immigration restrictions.
The provided source text contains only navigation and header information from the Census Bureau page and does not include the population figure of 3,929,214 for the 1790 census.
The provided source contains only navigation and a redirect notice, with no actual article content about the Emergency Quota Act.
The source explicitly states that 23,068 people arrived in 1933, matching the claim.
rows.source_quote: In 1933 just 23,068 arrived, the lowest number since 1831 and the record for this century.

rows.comments: The source confirms the year and number but does not specify that the immigration was European, so the claim is not fully supported.
rows.source_quote: Immigration reached an all-time high, with 8,795,386 for the decade, and 1,285,349 in 1907 alone.

rows.comments: The source reports that the STC still controls Aden, contradicting the claim that the group was dissolved and its forces collapsed after the capture.

rows.comments: The source provides specific migration figures that total roughly 385,000, supporting the claim of about 400,000 English migrants to America in the 17th century.
rows.source_quote: During the seventeenth century, emergent societies of the English Atlantic were transformed by large-scale migrations of hundreds of thousands of white settlers. Approximately 210,000 went to the Caribbean, 130,000 to the Chesapeake (Virginia and Maryland), 24,000 to the Middle Colonies, and 21,000 to New England.

rows.comments: The article discusses fighting in Aden involving Houthi militiamen and forces loyal to President Hadi, but it does not mention a "Battle of Aden" or the acronym PLC, so the claim is not supported by the source.
The article states that on 7 January (Wednesday) Saudi-backed forces moved toward Aden and that the coalition launched air strikes against secessionist forces, directly supporting the claim.
rows.source_quote: Saudi-backed ground forces on Wednesday moved on the Yemeni city of Aden, a stronghold of the southern secessionists supported by the United Arab Emirates (UAE). ... The Saudi Arabia-led coalition launched air strikes on southern Yemen saying it targeted secessionist forces after their leader disappeared instead of boarding a plane scheduled to take him to talks in Riyadh.

rows.comments: The article mentions Aden being declared a temporary capital in 2015, but it does not state that Aden has changed hands several times during the civil war.
The source reports that government forces entered Aden from Al‑Alam, but it contains no mention of Saudi airstrikes on 7 January 2026 against UAE‑backed STC forces.
The source confirms Aden was captured, the secretary‑general announced dissolution, and the leader fled to the UAE, matching the claim.
rows.source_quote: The turmoil follows an advance last month by STC forces into the governorates of Hadramout and al-Mahra, where they seized oil-rich areas and facilities and the presidential palace in the main southern city of Aden ... Yemen's main separatist group and its institutions will be dismantled effective Friday, the group's secretary-general said, following weeks of unrest in areas of southern Yemen and a day after its leader fled to the United Arab Emirates.

rows.source_quote: Al-Zubaidi did not board the plane and 'fled to an unknown location', it said. His current whereabouts remain unclear.

rows.comments: The source reports exactly 60 deaths, not more than 60.
rows.source_quote: The death toll from deadly clashes between Yemeni army forces and Shiite Houthi militants in northern Sanaa has risen to 60, a security source said Friday.

rows.comments: The article reports mass demonstrations in Sanaa demanding reversal of fuel subsidy cuts and resignation, and notes a meeting where the Houthis rejected government concessions.
rows.source_quote: Tens of thousands of Yemenis massed in the capital Sanaa on Friday in a protest called by the Shi'ite Houthi movement, which wants the government to reverse a decision on cutting fuel subsidies and resign. Representatives from the Houthis and the government had met on Thursday to try to reach an agreement to defuse tensions. "The disagreement focused on ... the Houthis' demand to set up a political party and join a new government (but) leaving out the issue of reversing a decision on fuel subsidies. The Houthis rejected that," a source in the government committee told Reuters on Thursday.

rows.comments: The source mentions the UN secretary‑general’s envoy announcing an agreement, but it does not mention Benomar or that he announced an agreement to end the crisis.
The source states the capture occurred on 22 September, not by 21 September, contradicting the claim.

rows.comments: The source confirms that Al‑Ahmer’s forces surrendered after fighting, but it does not mention the takeover of the prime minister’s office, state television building, or military headquarters.

rows.comments: The source contains all three elements of the claim verbatim.
rows.source_quote: Hours before the signing ceremony Prime Minister Mohammed Basindwa submitted his resignation to President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi, saying he hoped the move would help consensus emerge from the accord ... Witnesses at the ceremony said the Houthi representatives, who flew to Sanaa on a special flight from Saada, some 540 km (330 miles) to the north, refused to sign an annex to the accord which calls for the state to take control of areas seized by the Houthis and to return weapons captured during the fighting ... Despite the refusal of the Houthis -- and the small Nasserite party -- to sign the annex, Hadi immediately declared a ceasefire. 'I call on all parties to work together to implement the terms of this agreement from this moment,' he said in a televised speech.

Thus only part of the claim is supported.

rows.comments: The source states Hooker’s sermon in 1638 inspired the Fundamental Orders, which established a civil government and ensured Connecticut’s independence from Massachusetts, and that the Orders were the legal basis for the colony until the 1662 charter.
rows.source_quote: In 1638, Hooker preached a sermon on the text, “Choose men of wisdom, understanding, and repute…and [the Lord] will set them in authority over you,” arguing that the people of Connecticut had the right to choose their own government. The Fundamental Orders served as the legal basis for the Connecticut Colony until Charles II granted it a formal charter in 1662.

rows.comments: The source confirms all elements of the claim: renovation period, number of floors, hotel operator, apartments, restaurant, glass bar, and art gallery.
rows.source_quote: Two floors that had previously been used as an art gallery were converted over five months into hotel rooms that offer views of Prague Castle or the Vltava River. The hotel is operated by Luxury Suites s.r.o. ... The highlight for guests are apartments in the towers named the Ginger Royal Suite and Fred Royal Suite. For breakfast with a view, guests can relax in the Ginger & Fred restaurant, located on the seventh floor. We also cooperate with Glass Bar and the art gallery.

rows.comments: The source contains definitive statements that directly support each element of the claim.
rows.source_quote: By 2005, the Bush administration’s displeasure with Al‑Jazeera was so intense that it was straining the U.S.’s relationship with Qatar, an important ally in the region, and Qatari officials were considering selling off the station, The New York Times reported . That same year, Qatar hired Barbour Griffith & Rogers, the lobbying and public relations firm founded by Haley Barbour, on a $300,000 contract to improve relations with the Bush administration, according to O‘Dwyer’s PR Daily. “The PR campaign, to a certain degree, was successful,” said Suhail Khan, who served in the White House Office of Public Liaison during the Bush administration. “They just began booking Republican guests.”

rows.comments: The source confirms the date, the five New England states involved, and that secession was discussed, but it does not mention Maine being part of Massachusetts, so the claim is only partially supported.

The more extreme delegates raised the possibility of secession, but others sought only to dictate amendments to the Constitution that would protect their interests.
